title: THE ONE-OFF COVID EPIC: Warning- This episode has very little to do with AI!
description: Send us Fan Mail In a departure from normal programming Jimmy gives Matt the opportunity to scratch his Covid-19 itch and to introduce a pretty wild hypothesis about Covid, the long term effects of the brain and the need for Artificial Intelligence to mitigate this. It's something of an epic as Jimmy attempts to challenge some of Matt's more extreme views, but it also includes references to references to emerging studies and some hopeful ideas for ways to live a healthier life and mitigate some of then impacts. We do start with 20 minutes of AI as we touch on Donald Trump's recent presidential victory, his unexpected alliance with Elon Musk, and what it means for the future of AI governance and free speech on social media. We also look at whether the exponential growth of large language models coming to an end? Gary Marcus argues that AI might have hit a plateau, and we dig into this claim by examining differing opinions from industry leaders like Sam Altman and Mark Andreessen. While some predict revolutionary breakthroughs, others warn of the risks in over-relying on LLMs, especially with China exploring alternative strategies. This discussion challenges the current AI hype and invites listeners to critically assess whether the U.S.'s LLM-centric approach may lead to unforeseen global consequences. In our epic deep dive COVID-19's long shadow looms large, affecting cognitive function and societal health. We explore how the pandemic and it's management is having a lasting impact on education and mental health, drawing parallels with other viral infections. We somewhat tenuously consider AI's potential role in addressing these challenges. From the decline in ACT scores to ongoing debates about COVID's long-term cognitive effects. As we consider practical strategies for managing COVID exposure and its societal impact, the conversation underscores the importance of informed action and collective resilience.
summary: Matt's promised COVID episode: he argues the pandemic's medium-to-long-term effects — autoimmune disease, immune damage and measurable cognitive decline — are being ignored, citing falling ACT scores and a 113,000-person New England Journal of Medicine study. Jimmy pushes back on causation and extrapolation but agrees lingering effects could last decades, and Matt lands his tenuous AI link: society may need AI to cover jobs as cognition and health decline.
keyTalkingPoints: Matt outlines four claimed effects of COVID or the vaccines: autoimmune disease, immune-system damage, brain damage and long-term sickness
US ACT math scores fell to their lowest ever recorded around 2021-22; symptomatic COVID patients in one study showed cognitive decline equivalent to 10.6 years of aging
Economic inactivity in the UK has risen 900,000 since 2020, 85% attributed to long-term sickness; US self-reported disability has more than doubled since 2019
Jimmy counters that correlation is not causation, past pandemics like Spanish flu had knock-on effects, and recovery could take 20-30 years
Matt's hot take: COVID-driven intelligence loss at societal scale means AI will be needed to perform cognitively demanding jobs and replace workers lost to chronic illness

jimmy: COVID's long-term effects are plausible — new crossover viruses always have knock-on effects — but recovery will take 20 to 30 years, like past pandemics
Linking disability statistics directly to COVID is very difficult; correlation is not causation

LLMs approximate human output on the internet; reaching 100% of that is not AGI
matt: COVID and the mRNA shots are driving chronic illness, cognitive decline and workforce loss that society is refusing to face
A societal day of reckoning over COVID is coming within about three years, faster than the AIDS reckoning took
AI will be needed to mitigate intelligence loss and replace workers who leave the workforce with chronic conditions
